queries_attempted: WhatsApp API media support images videos documents
WhatsApp web js media upload issues
WhatsApp unofficial API media handling solution

competitors.name: whatsapp-web.js
competitors.notes: Most popular unofficial WhatsApp Web automation library. Provides media sending (images, videos, documents, audio) but has known inconsistencies: certain file types fail, size limits vary, and encoding issues require custom workarounds. Not purpose-built for reliable media handling; media support is a secondary feature.
competitors.feature_overlap: Sending images, videos, documents, audio via WhatsApp Web. Supports media upload and download.
competitors.market_positioning: General-purpose WhatsApp automation library for developers.

competitors.name: Baileys
competitors.notes: Another popular unofficial WhatsApp Web library. Similar media handling capabilities with reported issues for certain media types (e.g., stickers, documents with specific MIME types). Inconsistent across WhatsApp protocol versions.
competitors.feature_overlap: Media sending and receiving, including images, videos, documents, and audio.

competitors.name: Venom
competitors.notes: Unofficial WhatsApp automation library. Media handling similar to whatsapp-web.js but with its own set of bugs and limitations. Not actively maintained as of late 2023.
competitors.feature_overlap: Media sending (images, videos, documents) via WhatsApp Web.
competitors.market_positioning: WhatsApp automation with focus on multi-device support.

competitors.name: WhatsApp Business API (Cloud API)
competitors.notes: Official WhatsApp Business API. Reliable media handling but with strict constraints: max 16MB for images, 100MB for videos, limited document types, and requires business verification. Not suitable for personal or small-scale automation. Different approach (official API vs. unofficial Web automation).
competitors.feature_overlap: Sending and receiving media messages with guaranteed delivery and format support within limits.
competitors.pricing: Per conversation (free tier available, then $0.005-0.08 per conversation depending on region)

competitors.name: Twilio WhatsApp API
competitors.notes: Uses official WhatsApp Business API under the hood. Same media constraints as Cloud API. Provides reliable media handling but limited to official API capabilities. Not a direct competitor for unofficial automation use cases.
competitors.feature_overlap: Media messaging via WhatsApp with Twilio's abstraction layer.
competitors.pricing: Per message ($0.005 per message + media costs)
competitors.market_positioning: Cloud communications platform with WhatsApp integration.

competitors.name: WATI
competitors.notes: WhatsApp automation platform (SaaS). Includes media sending as part of its features. Relies on official WhatsApp Business API. Not a library or tool for developers to integrate into their own code; it's a full platform.
competitors.feature_overlap: Send images, videos, documents via WhatsApp automation.
competitors.market_positioning: No-code WhatsApp marketing and support platform.

competitors.name: ChatAPI
competitors.notes: WhatsApp API service that uses unofficial methods (similar to whatsapp-web.js). Provides media sending but with similar inconsistencies. Not a dedicated media handling solution.

competitors.name: Ultramsg
competitors.notes: Another WhatsApp API service. Media handling capabilities but dependent on underlying unofficial WhatsApp Web protocol. Inconsistent support for media types and sizes.

competitors.name: whatsapp-media-downloader (npm)
competitors.notes: Niche npm package for downloading media from WhatsApp Web. Only handles download side, not sending. Very limited scope.
competitors.market_positioning: Utility for extracting media from WhatsApp.

competitors.name: CloudConvert
competitors.notes: Media conversion service. Can be used to pre-process media to supported formats before sending via WhatsApp. Not specific to WhatsApp automation; a general tool.
competitors.feature_overlap: Converting media files to WhatsApp-compatible formats.

summary: The competitive landscape for reliable, consistent media handling in WhatsApp automation is weak. The most common approach is using unofficial libraries (whatsapp-web.js, Baileys, Venom) which provide basic media support but are plagued by inconsistencies across media types, sizes, and formats. Developers frequently resort to custom encoding/decoding logic, manual upload/download handling, and retry mechanisms. Official APIs (WhatsApp Business API, Twilio) offer reliability but are limited to business accounts, have strict size and format constraints, and are not suitable for unofficial automation use cases. No purpose-built library or service exists that specifically solves the problem of abstracting away media handling inconsistencies in WhatsApp automation. The gap is significant: developers need a drop-in solution that handles all media types and sizes reliably, without custom workarounds.
